reasons_add: Ibn al-Jawzī transmits al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās on the signs as landmarks.
Ibn al-Jawzī attributes the mountain identification to Ibn al-Sāʾib and Muqātil.
Ibn al-Jawzī attributes the division between stellar markers and guiding stars to Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Nakhaʿī.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah prefers the generic sense after mentioning other identifications. He also calls an earlier explanation weak, but its content is not preserved in this excerpt, so the object of his criticism cannot be identified. Ibn al-Jawzī reports al-Zajjāj's generic-singular explanation.
Ibn al-Jawzī transmits al-Māwardī's identification of al-Jady as the most fixed star at its center.
Ibn al-Jawzī transmits al-Suddī's set: the Pleiades, the two Farqads, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
Ibn ʿAṭiyyah transmits al-Farrāʾ's identification of al-Jady and the two Farqads; Ibn al-Jawzī also attributes it to Ibn al-Sāʾib.
Ibn ʿAṭiyyah reports an unnamed identification with the Pole Star, specified as unmoving.
Ibn al-Jawzī attributes the reading with ḍamma on both nūn and jīm to al-Jaḥdarī.
Ibn al-Jawzī also attributes the nūn-ḍamma, jīm-sukūn reading to al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū al-Mutawakkil, alongside al-Ḥasan and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb.

question: 16:16/q05
position: Mujāhid reads the full plural al-nujūm, retaining its wāw.
reasons: Ibn al-Jawzī reports this reading from Mujāhid.

reasons_add: Ibn al-Jawzī transmits al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās on navigation by stars at night; he also reports travel guidance as one interpretation of the clause.
Ibn al-Jawzī reports finding the direction of prayer as the other interpretation of stellar guidance.
Al-Durr transmits Ibrāhīm's view that there is no harm in learning enough of the stars to navigate by them.
